  "summary": "S1 — Outcome (fact): a small single-player Battleship game playable in a browser against a computer opponent. Entry point and consumer (fact): one person uses the browser; the browser-accessible application is the named target and grant for delivery. Interaction and state defaults (assumptions): one anonymous player per browser session, no account or cross-device identity; game state belongs to that session, is held in memory, and ends on reset, reload, or server restart; the player does not see the computer's unhit ships through the game interface. These defaults rule out multiplayer, persistence, session recovery, and a security guarantee against inspecting application data. Discovery must first establish what the runtime already provides; the recorded defaults answer identity, sharing, lifetime, and visibility questions if no existing capabilities apply, and block the interaction and state design until resolved. Rules default (assumption): use conventional Battleship rules and a simple computer opponent; discovery should establish any existing rule or design guidance first, after which this default unblocks gameplay design. Risk: ship concealment and turn handling need verification. S2 — Outcome (fact): use a Node.js server and include tests. Test default (assumption): exercise core game rules and the server's browser entry point; discovery must first establish available tooling, and this default unblocks test selection. Run boundary (fact): the repository is empty, this stage implements nothing, and no deployment target is specified. Discovery source hints (leads, not verified facts): inspect the workspace and any available project guidance for runtime, tooling, and Battleship rule conventions; no team, channel, internal site, private repository, owner, or sensitive locator is named. Visibility (fact): in an isolated run, its source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; any deployed outcome becomes visible only after release. No person-only step is currently required."
}
